quietEq.text:
Voice Check Bench · suggested settings
Based on: Control · 8 cm · raw (speech -40.0 dBFS, noise -80 dBFS)
Keep the mic at 8 cm. Point the capsule at your mouth. Leave the Wave XLR gain where it was for this take.

FIRST: The raw take is quiet (-40 dBFS). Raise the Wave XLR gain about 10 dB first, then record the control takes again. The gate and compressor values depend on it.

Wave XLR (hardware)
  Lowcut Filter: on, 120 Hz

Effects order: ReaGate → ReaEQ → ReaComp

ReaGate
  Threshold: -68 dB
  Attack: 1 ms
  Hold: 150 ms
  Release: 200 ms
  Hysteresis: -6 dB
  Wet: 0 dB
  Dry: -20 dB

ReaEQ (use these bands only; remove or disable any others)
  Band 1: Type Low Shelf · Frequency 150 Hz · Gain -6.5 dB · Bandwidth 2.00 oct   (Boom +9.4 dB on the raw mic)
  Band 2: Type Band · Frequency 3500 Hz · Gain +4.5 dB · Bandwidth 1.40 oct   (Presence -6.6 dB)

ReaComp
  Threshold: -45 dB
  Ratio: 3:1
  Attack: 5 ms
  Release: 100 ms
  Knee size: 6 dB
  Wet (makeup): +18 dB
  Limit output: on

Elgato De-Esser: off
Voice Focus, Elgato EQ, Elgato Noise Removal: off

noisyCondenserSide.text:
Voice Check Bench · suggested settings
Based on: Control · 8 cm · raw (speech -22.0 dBFS, noise -40 dBFS)
Keep the mic at 8 cm. Speak into the front side of the mic (usually where the logo is), not the top. Leave the Wave XLR gain where it was for this take.

FIRST: The input is noisy: the room/input noise (-40 dBFS) is only 18 dB under your voice. No gate or EQ setting can separate them, and the gate would cut quiet words. Get the most out of the room: Keep the loudest noise at the mic's sides, about 125° off-axis. Speak closer and switch off what you can, then set up the noise-reduction step below before the EQ. Re-record the control takes to check: the closer to 30 dB, the cleaner. Condenser mics pick up more of the room: stay closer and lower the gain.

Wave XLR (hardware)
  Lowcut Filter: on, 80 Hz

Effects order: ReaFIR → ReaEQ → ReaComp → ReaGate

ReaFIR (noise reduction)
  1. In Wave Link → your mic → Effects, add "ReaFIR (ReaPlugs Edition)" and drag it to the top.
  2. Mode: Subtract. FFT size: 4096.
  3. Stay silent, tick "Automatically build noise profile" for about 3 seconds, then untick it.
  4. Drag the whole curve down a little (about 6 dB), then talk and listen. Stop at the first watery or robotic sound; if it never sounds clean, use an AI noise remover instead.
  5. Keep ReaEQ, ReaComp and ReaGate below ReaFIR, in that order.
  6. After noise removal your voice may get quieter: raise ReaComp Wet by the same amount (the results show how much).
  Alternatives: Elgato Noise Removal (in Wave Link), Voice Focus by ai-coustics (in Wave Link), NVIDIA Broadcast — Noise Removal (RTX GPUs)

ReaEQ (use these bands only; remove or disable any others)
  Band 1: Type High Shelf · Frequency 10000 Hz · Gain -2.0 dB · Bandwidth 2.00 oct   (Room noise dominates above 5 kHz)
  Band 2: Type Band (notch) · Frequency 6200 Hz · Gain -12.0 dB · Bandwidth 0.10 oct   (Fan/machine tone +30.0 dB)
  Band 3: Type Band (notch) · Frequency 410 Hz · Gain -11.0 dB · Bandwidth 0.10 oct   (Fan/machine tone +22.0 dB)
  Band 4: Type Band (notch) · Frequency 1830 Hz · Gain -6.5 dB · Bandwidth 0.10 oct   (Fan/machine tone +13.0 dB)

ReaComp
  Threshold: -26 dB
  Ratio: 2.5:1
  Attack: 5 ms
  Release: 100 ms
  Knee size: 6 dB
  Wet (makeup): +4 dB
  Limit output: on

ReaGate
  Threshold: -52 dB
  Attack: 1 ms
  Hold: 200 ms
  Release: 300 ms
  Hysteresis: -6 dB
  Wet: 0 dB
  Dry: -10 dB

Elgato De-Esser: on (light)
Elgato EQ: off. Use only one noise remover: ReaFIR, or one of the alternatives above (not both).
